why: Two printed lines, the second with a lower-case 'house' and a list that runs to the end of the data; only the first has a spoken total (report 37957, 22 December 1965).
rows: As the Prime Minister has already indicated, under the provisions of Article 90 of the Constitution of the State of Singapore, this Bill as it now stands before the House shall not be passed by the Legislative Assembly unless it has been supported on Second and Third Readings by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Members thereof. It, therefore, means that the Bill now before the House requires the votes of not less than 34 Members on its Second and Third Readings. After I have put the Question and after the Division Bells have been rung for two minutes, the Clerk will call the names of Members in alphabetical order and record each Member's vote and the names of Members who abstain from voting.
Question put, "That the Bill be now read a Second Time."

36 Ayes, 15 Absent. I declare that under Article 90 of the Constitution of the State of Singapore the Second Reading has been carried by not less than two-thirds of the total number of Members of the House.
Bill accordingly read a Second time and committed to a Committee of the whole Assembly.
Assembly immediately resolved itself into a Committee on the Bill. - [The Prime Minister].
Bill considered in Committee; reported without amendment.
I beg to move, "That the Bill be now read a Third time."
Question put, "That the Bill be now read a Third time."
The procedure that was adopted on the Second Reading will again he adopted on this Bill. The Clerk will ring the Division Bells.
Barker, E. W.       Chan Sun Wing
